mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25 percentage points over the past 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 60-day moving average during high-rate regimes (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with the combined labor indicators (Pearson IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% suggests expanding domestic demand, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports S&P 500 positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During high-inflation periods, SPX 20-day returns do not outperform the 5-day moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in the goods price index (not available in the provided catalog) would typically signal supply shock, but here we proxy with a sharp drop in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) of > 1% in a month, predicting negative S&P 500 20-day returns due to inflation expectations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by > 1% in a single month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain positive despite CPIAUCSL decline (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 3% for three consecutive months, it indicates accommodative policy, which lowers real discount rates and supports higher S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 60 days, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (not available) but here we use a surge in payrolls (PAYEMS) of > 50,000 jobs in a month combined with a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) crossing 4%, signaling a transition to labor market cooling and a negative 20-day SPX forecast.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 50,000 jobs while UNRATE rises above 4% in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain positive despite the cooling indicators (Pearson IC > -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 3% suggests weakening demand or supply constraints, which typically precedes a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day moving average during such periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% while the federal funds rate remains unchanged for two months, it creates policy divergence that can erode equity valuations, producing a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and FEDFUNDS unchanged for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such regimes, SPX 5-day returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).
